newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie to lose European Parliament seat.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie to lose European Parliament seat.

text.p: France will notify the European Parliament next week that bankrupt ex-businessman and soccer boss Bernard Tapie must be deprived of his seat in the assembly, French officials said on Friday.
Tapie, declared by a court to be bankrupt and ineligible for public office, has already been ejected from the French National Assembly and must give up his European seat for the same reason.
Officials said a decree depriving him of his European seat, signed by Prime Minister Alain Juppe, would be sent next week to the president of the Strasbourg assembly, Klaus Haensch of Germany.
Under European Union law, the laws of individual member states determine eligibility for the European parliament, French authorities say.
Tapie would be able to appeal against the decision to the European Parliament and France's Council of State, its highest administrative court.

Tapie, target of a blizzard of legal actions over his now-destroyed business empire and the Marseille soccer team he once ran, has been sentenced to jail terms of eight and six months for tax fraud and rigging a soccer match.
He is appealing in both cases to the Supreme Court.
